answer: Agents secure access by executing a memory-hard computation across 1,000 megabytes of shale, a task requiring massive RAM footprint. An honest participant spends this effort once, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000,000 units to bypass the verifier. The system uses a karst algorithm to detect memory-access collisions, acting as a bridge to reject pooled hardware. We assume individual compute cannot be amortized or shared.
